title: Zampini 2005 Experiment 3 · electrocutaneous touch
citation: Zampini, M., Brown, T., Shore, D. I., Maravita, A., Röder, B., & Spence, C. (2005). Audiotactile temporal order judgments. Acta Psychologica, 118(3), 277–291.
notes: The 40-cell auditory inspection shows nominal timing and side pairs. Electrical calibration and the final test schedule remain unresolved.

participants.cohort: Experienced observers. Six also took part in Experiment 2.

apparatus.auditory: Two Audax VE100AO speakers immediately behind the respective tactile sites. White-noise bursts last 9 ms, with nominal level 82 dBA at the head.

tactile.actuator: STM140, H.T.L., with one electrode at each finger pad

published_trial_schedule.sign_rule: Sound onset minus tactile onset. Negative values indicate sound-first trials.
published_trial_schedule.allocation_note: The Experiment 3 report refers to a similar procedure and comparable trial counts. Its exact test and practice allocation is unconfirmed.
published_trial_schedule.timing_scope_note: The nominal timing grid is adopted from the referenced Experiments 1–2 procedure with a source caveat.

intensity_setting.criterion: Individual perceptible, nonpainful stimulation on the index finger pads.

response.device: Normally depressed right-foot toe and heel pedals

analysis.primary_measure: Temporal-order judgment. Fit the normal-score transform of touch-first proportions separately by participant and side alignment.

inspection_scope.auditory_spatialization: Toolkit stereo pan at the two reported azimuths.
inspection_scope.details: One auditory inspection per nominal SOA and side pairing. The 40 displayed cells are an inspection grid chosen for this profile. The publication leaves exact Experiment 3 counts unresolved. Digital, stationary sound bursts and nominal order combinations only. The touch side and lead are annotations; there is no tactile output, independent masker, fixation-light hardware or response scoring. Auditory onset is scheduled from an implicit fixation at the row start. The toolkit SOA control measures a nonnegative delay from sound onset. Touch-first timing remains a planned value.

implementation_gaps: The trial scheduler requires independent auditory and tactile triggers for signed temporal orders plus light feedback. This profile schedules only the auditory member of each pair.
Speaker and tactile calibration must verify delivered intensity and acoustic-to-skin onset. Original waveform bytes and measured timing are unavailable.
The tactile apparatus uses a two-site electrocutaneous stimulator with individual nonpainful calibration. The printed voltage range does not supply the pulse waveform, width or delivered current.
Exact Experiment 3 per-block, per-cell and practice trial allocations are unreported. The inspection uses one auditory presentation per nominal cell.

provenance.field: Cohort, speaker setup, tactile stimulus, trial order and response
Comparison timing, apparatus geometry and temporal-order scoring
